description: Composite group of three images. The top image is a table of mechanical properties with columns Steel, Condition, YS (MPa), UTS (MPa), TE (%), KU2 (J) and KIC (MPa·m^1/2) for the 0Al and 1.3Al steels in as-quenched (WQ) and 2 h tempered conditions: 0Al WQ 1234±22, 2294±9, 9.5±0.6, 33±6; 0Al 2 h 1400±12, 1925±5, 13.5±1.8, 65±3, KIC 97.6; 1.3Al WQ 1113±11, 2145±144, 4.3±0.9, 23±2; 1.3Al 2 h 1272±52, 1876±25, 13.7±0.4, 80±3, KIC 108.0; WQ KIC entries are dashes. Panel (a) is a SEM micrograph of the 1.3Al steel (10 µm scale bar, bottom-left) showing a tempered martensitic lath/plate structure with many differently oriented packets crossing at various angles; a yellow-framed inset (0.2 µm scale bar) shows dark elongated bands in a lighter matrix. Panel (b) shows two vertically offset XRD patterns, Intensity (no numeric scale) versus 2θ (20-110°, ticks at 20, 40, 60, 80, 100°), for 0Al steel (upper, blue) and 1.3Al steel (lower, purple), with peaks labelled (110)α, (111)γ, (200)α, (200)γ, (211)α, (220)α and printed dislocation densities ρ0Al ≈ 2.01×10^15 m^-2 and ρ1.3Al ≈ 2.20×10^15 m^-2. Together the group links microstructure (a) and phase/dislocation state (b) to the property table.

observations.observation: The table reports YS, UTS, TE, KU2 and KIC for two steels (0Al, 1.3Al) in two conditions (WQ and 2 h temper).
0Al steel in the 2 h tempered condition gives YS 1400 ± 12 MPa, UTS 1925 ± 5 MPa, TE 13.5 ± 1.8 %, KU2 65 ± 3 J and KIC 97.6 MPa·m^1/2.
1.3Al steel in the 2 h tempered condition gives YS 1272 ± 52 MPa, UTS 1876 ± 25 MPa, TE 13.7 ± 0.4 %, KU2 80 ± 3 J and KIC 108.0 MPa·m^1/2.
KIC is listed only for the 2 h tempered state (97.6 for 0Al; 108.0 for 1.3Al); the WQ rows contain a dash instead of a value.
In the as-quenched (WQ) state the 0Al steel shows higher UTS (2294 ± 9 MPa) than the 1.3Al steel (2145 ± 144 MPa), and lower TE (9.5 ± 0.6 % versus 4.3 ± 0.9 %).
2 h tempering increases KU2 for both steels (33 ± 6 J to 65 ± 3 J for 0Al; 23 ± 2 J to 80 ± 3 J for 1.3Al) and lowers UTS, while KE/TE rises.
Panel (a) is a SEM micrograph of the 1.3Al steel with a 10 µm scale bar, showing a tempered martensitic lath/plate structure with multiple differently oriented packet variants.
The yellow-framed inset in panel (a) carries a 0.2 µm scale bar and shows dark elongated bands within a lighter, mottled matrix.
Panel (b) plots XRD Intensity (no numeric scale given) versus 2θ from 20 to about 110°, with ticks at 20, 40, 60, 80 and 100°.
XRD peaks are labelled (110)α (dominant, near 45°), (111)γ, (200)α, (200)γ, (211)α and (220)α; the two patterns are vertically offset and labelled '0Al steel' (upper) and '1.3Al steel' (lower).
Dislocation densities are printed inside panel (b) as ρ0Al ≈ 2.01×10^15 m^-2 (blue, upper pattern) and ρ1.3Al ≈ 2.20×10^15 m^-2 (purple, lower pattern).
The caption states the table gives YS, UTS, TE and impact absorption energy (KU2) of the 0Al and 1.3Al steels in the as quenched (WQ) and 2 h tempered conditions.
The caption states Fig. 2(a) is the microstructure of the 1.3Al steel and Fig. 2(b) the XRD patterns of the 0Al and 1.3Al steels.
The citing text states both the 0Al and 1.3Al steels exhibit tempered martensitic structures and that a small amount of retained austenite remains in both steels after tempering.

The citing text states retained austenite contents of 1.8 % (1.3Al) and 1.0 % (0Al), and dislocation densities of ~2.20×10^15 m^-2 (1.3Al) and ~2.01×10^15 m^-2 (0Al) obtained by the Williamson-Hall approach on the (110)M, (200)M and (211) peaks.

subfigures.description: Property table (rendered as an image) listing Steel (0Al, 1.3Al), Condition (WQ, 2 h), YS (MPa), UTS (MPa), TE (%), KU2 (J) and KIC (MPa·m^1/2), each with ± errors; KIC is reported only for the 2 h tempered conditions (97.6 for 0Al, 108.0 for 1.3Al) and shown as a dash for WQ.

SEM micrograph of the 1.3Al steel with a 10 µm scale bar, showing a tempered martensitic lath/plate (needle-like packet) structure with differently oriented variants. A yellow-framed inset at 0.2 µm scale bar shows dark elongated features in a lighter mottled matrix.

Two vertically stacked XRD patterns, Intensity versus 2θ (20-110°), for 0Al steel (upper, blue) and 1.3Al steel (lower, purple); sharp dominant (110)α reflection near 45° plus weaker (200)α, (211)α, (220)α and small (111)γ, (200)γ reflections; dislocation densities printed on the panel.
